sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Benin
sources.temporal_coverage: EHCVM household survey 2018/19; climate projections including 2070
sources.methodology: CCDR analysis with EHCVM 2018/19 household shock estimates.
sources.limitations: EHCVM shocks are self-reported retrospectively; fragility passage gives no causal estimate.

sources.title: Benin Economic Update 2024: Adapting to climate change for sustainable, resilient economic growth
sources.temporal_coverage: Economic-loss projection through 2050; adaptation priorities for coming decades
sources.methodology: World Bank publisher summary of the 2024 Economic Update; projected losses are reported as estimates.
sources.limitations: The inspected summary does not state the model assumptions or climate scenario behind the GDP estimate.

sources.title: Troisième Contribution Déterminée au niveau National du Bénin (CDN 3.0)
geographic_coverage: Coastal zone and five seafront communes
sources.temporal_coverage: Agricultural statistics through 2025; climate risks and planned adaptation measures in NDC 3.0
sources.methodology: Government NDC submission describing sectoral climate vulnerabilities, exposure and planned projects.
sources.limitations: Project listings are commitments, not evidence of implementation or effectiveness; coastal erosion rates apply to critical locations.

claims.locator: PDF p. 18 (one-based), paragraph beginning ‘Climatic pressures are set to aggravate’.
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR says climatic pressures could widen rural-urban and north-south gaps, compounding northern insecurity and displacement, including Sahelian in-migration.
claims.scenario: No scenario or numeric horizon specified.
affected_groups: People exposed to insecurity in northern Benin
claims.limitations: Stated risk pathway; no causal estimate or displacement attribution.

claims.locator: Chapter 5, section 5.1.1, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 64), EHCVM 2018/19 household-shock paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: In EHCVM 2018/19, 21.4% of households reported a climate-induced shock during the previous three years; 10.5% reported flood impacts and 12% drought impacts.
claims.limitations: Retrospective self-report; flood and drought shares may overlap.

claims.locator: Chapter 5, section 5.1.1, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 64), paragraphs on differential household impacts.
claims.paraphrase: Poor, rural and agriculture-reliant households reported greater exposure to climate shocks; over 36% of agriculture-reliant households reported flood and/or drought impacts, versus about 21% overall.
claims.limitations: Historical self-report; subgroup differences are not causal estimates.

claims.locator: Chapter 1, section 1.2, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 18), projected extreme-temperature exposure paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR projects that by 2070, 98% of Benin’s territory could face extreme temperatures under a 2.7°C global-warming pathway associated with current policies.
claims.scenario: 2.7°C global warming under current policies, as stated in the CCDR passage.
claims.limitations: Modelled exposure, not an observed temperature impact; retain the CCDR’s stated global-warming pathway.

claims.locator: Publisher summary, bullet on projected climate-related economic losses.
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank summary says average annual GDP losses from climate change could reach up to 19% by 2050 without additional adaptation.
claims.scenario: Without additional adaptation; the inspected summary does not specify the underlying climate scenario.
claims.limitations: Summary-level projection; underlying assumptions and uncertainty range were not available in the inspected passage.

claims.locator: Section 3, agriculture subsection, printed pp. 14–15 (PDF pp. 14–15), paragraphs on sector profile and CDN 3.0 projects.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports that agriculture employs about 70% of the population and accounts for 72.9% of export receipts; it identifies rainfall extremes, floods, dry spells, heat and strong winds as risks and lists 30 sectoral plus 51 commune-led adaptation projects.
claims.limitations: Economic figures refer to the period stated in the NDC; project counts describe plans, not completed or effective measures.

claims.locator: Section 5.1.3, Littoral, printed pp. 51–52 (PDF pp. 49–50), coastal-risk description.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC identifies 30 communes in the coastal zone, five on the seafront, and reports shoreline retreat of 12–30 metres per year at critical points alongside flood, drought, wind and sea-level risks.
claims.limitations: The erosion rate is reported for critical points, not as a uniform rate along the coast.

sources.title: Ambitious climate action will reap large dividends for Cabo Verde
sources.temporal_coverage: Current vulnerabilities and GDP/tourism projections through 2050
sources.methodology: World Bank official CCDR summary page describing sectoral exposure and headline projections.
sources.limitations: Summary page omits assumptions behind 2050 estimates.

sources.title: Cabo Verde Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0 (NDC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate trends over approximately 50 years; current vulnerability assessment
sources.methodology: Government NDC summarizing historical climate analysis and differentiated vulnerability assessments.
sources.limitations: The cited vulnerability passages are national diagnostics; station-level and group-level methods are not detailed there.

sources.title: Cabo Verde: Increasing Resilience to Disasters and Climate-Related Shocks
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank-supported disaster-risk reforms reported for 2018–2022
sources.methodology: World Bank results brief describing a policy-financing operation and reported outputs.
sources.limitations: Institutional achievements are publisher-reported results; the page does not provide an independent counterfactual evaluation.

claims.locator: ‘A Growing Threat’ section, paragraph 1.
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank summary says sea-level rise threatens coastlines on which much of Cabo Verde’s tourism depends.
claims.scenario: Not specified in inspected summary.
claims.limitations: Summary risk only; no island-specific exposure estimate.

claims.locator: ‘A Growing Threat’ section, paragraph 1.
claims.paraphrase: The summary identifies drought and saline intrusion as threats to agriculture, income and food security in rural communities of this water-scarce country.
claims.scenario: Not specified in inspected summary.
claims.limitations: Summary gives no affected-household or island breakdown.

claims.locator: ‘A Growing Threat’ section, paragraph 1.
claims.paraphrase: The summary identifies warming oceans and overfishing as threats to fisheries, which accounted for 72% of exports in 2021.
claims.limitations: Export share is for 2021; effects are not separated.

claims.locator: ‘A Growing Threat’ section, paragraph 2.
claims.paraphrase: Without action, the CCDR summary projects GDP could be up to 3.6% smaller in 2050 and tourism revenue up to 10% lower.
claims.scenario: Without action; climate scenario unspecified.
claims.limitations: Headline projection; assumptions and uncertainty range omitted.

claims.locator: Section 2.2.1, ‘Historical Climate Trends’, printed p. 11 (PDF pp. 21–22).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports about 0.14°C warming per decade (roughly 0.7°C over 50 years); rainfall is highly variable and has no statistically significant long-term national trend.
claims.limitations: NDC summary of historical analysis; local stations show variation and should not be read as uniform island-level trends.

claims.locator: Section 8.1, ‘Vulnerable Groups and Climate Impacts’, printed pp. 73–74 (PDF pp. 84–85).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC says rural and peri-urban women in agriculture, water management and care face higher workloads and reduced income during prolonged drought and resource scarcity, while remaining underrepresented in climate governance.
claims.limitations: This is the NDC’s vulnerability assessment; the cited text gives no group-level quantitative estimate.

claims.locator: Section 8.1, ‘Vulnerable Groups and Climate Impacts’, printed pp. 73–74 (PDF pp. 84–85).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC identifies youth risks linked to limited jobs, education and decision participation, and children’s exposure to climate-related health risks, food insecurity and schooling disruption.
geographies: Areas with limited infrastructure and services
claims.limitations: NDC diagnostic statement; the passage does not provide disaggregated outcome estimates.

claims.locator: ‘Results’ section, paragraphs 1–3; Cat DDO-supported reforms during 2018–2022.
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank reports that hazard and climate-risk assessments were incorporated into municipal spatial-planning tools and that a Ministry of Finance risk service and National Emergency Fund were operationalized.
claims.limitations: World Bank results reporting for 2018–2022; does not independently evaluate effectiveness or impact on losses.

access_audit.notes: Opened official World Bank CCDR summary page; did not inspect the full CCDR PDF.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Côte d’Ivoire
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical 2018 flood example; cocoa and climate projections for the 2050s
sources.methodology: World Bank CCDR using sector analysis, climate projections and cited crop-suitability modelling.
sources.limitations: Cocoa table cites an external model without a stated scenario.

sources.title: Contribution Déterminée au niveau National 3.0 de la Côte d’Ivoire
sources.temporal_coverage: Current vulnerability assessment and adaptation planning in NDC 3.0
sources.methodology: Government NDC describing health, social and geographic climate vulnerabilities and planned adaptation measures.
sources.limitations: The cited passages summarize diagnosis and plans; implementation outcomes are not assessed there.

sources.title: The Climate Change and Conflict Nexus in West Africa: A New Approach for Operationally Relevant Vulnerability Assessments
sources.temporal_coverage: Qualitative case study drawing on country literature and interviews; no single projection horizon
sources.methodology: Qualitative Côte d’Ivoire case study triangulating literature, local and organizational reports, and semi-structured interviews.
sources.limitations: Identifies potential risks, not causal attribution; findings are context-specific and some evidence is qualitative.

claims.locator: Printed p. 60 (PDF p. 60), Table 1, climatic suitability levels for cocoa in the 2050s; source note cites Schroth et al. (2016).
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR’s cited projection shows land in Côte d’Ivoire rated over 50% suitable for cocoa falling by 57% in the 2050s, while lower-suitability classes expand.
claims.scenario: The inspected table does not specify the climate-model scenario.
claims.limitations: Suitability class, not yield; table cites Schroth et al. (2016).

claims.locator: PDF p. 37 (one-based; web index P36), printed p. 9, climate-risk bullet on migration, northern insecurity and resource competition.
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR says climate-related migration and more intense drought could add to north–south movement and herder–farmer competition over scarce land and water, with potential stability and recruitment implications in vulnerable rural areas.
claims.scenario: The inspected risk passage does not specify a climate scenario or numeric horizon.
claims.limitations: Possible pathway only; no causal estimate or observed recruitment effect.

claims.locator: Printed p. 65 (PDF p. 65), urban flood-risk discussion of Abidjan and June 2018 event.
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR reports severe flooding in Abidjan in June 2018, with more than 20 deaths, and identifies low-lying informal settlements and poorer residents among those exposed.
claims.limitations: The event is a dated example; it does not establish a climate-change attribution for the 2018 flood.

claims.locator: PDF p. 31, health and vulnerable-population paragraphs (lines 1858–1887 in the inspected text).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC links heat with increased malaria risk and floods or polluted water with cholera and diarrhoea, noting particular risks for children, older people and those with chronic illness where health capacity and access are limited.
claims.scenario: The inspected passage does not specify a climate scenario.
claims.limitations: Risk assessment does not quantify cases or state a scenario.

claims.locator: PDF p. 31, vulnerable-population paragraph (lines 1871–1887 in the inspected text).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports that women hold less than 20% of land and have substantially lower access to finance, while describing women, youth, children, older people and people with disabilities as especially vulnerable to climate impacts.
claims.limitations: Survey source and reference year are unstated.

claims.locator: PDF p. 83, adaptation-plan passage (lines 5789–5805 in the inspected text).
claims.paraphrase: NDC 3.0 plans northern pastoral measures, forest-zone agroforestry and coastal-erosion protection; these are not evaluated results.
claims.limitations: Planned actions only; delivery and effectiveness unassessed.

claims.locator: Côte d’Ivoire case study, printed p. 72 (PDF p. 70), summary of three potential climate-fragility risks.
claims.paraphrase: The qualitative case study identifies possible risks from large-scale environmental migration and community tensions, insecurity in economic, health and food systems, and increased herder–farmer conflict; it says these risks can be averted.
claims.scenario: The case-study summary does not specify a climate scenario or numeric horizon.
claims.limitations: Qualitative potential-risk assessment, not a causal finding; the authors state that appropriate policy can avert the risks.

sources.title: The Republic of Congo can turn the climate crisis into an opportunity to end poverty and boost shared prosperity
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank CCDR summary includes projections through 2050 and policy priorities
sources.methodology: World Bank press-release summary of the Republic of Congo CCDR and its headline estimates and recommendations.
sources.limitations: Summary page does not present the modeling assumptions behind economic-loss projections; recommendations are not outcomes.

sources.title: Contribution Déterminée au niveau National de la République du Congo
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Congo
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC vulnerability assessment and adaptation priorities; historical hydrological observations described in the document
sources.methodology: Government NDC describing sectoral vulnerability, observed impacts and planned adaptation actions.
sources.limitations: The cited assessment is dated 2021; it is not a current flood-impact inventory.

sources.title: Republic of Congo: Selected Issues; IMF Country Report No. 24/252
sources.temporal_coverage: EM-DAT data from 2000; flood events and government estimates for 2023–2024
sources.methodology: IMF selected-issues chapter uses EM-DAT, WFP and initial government estimates for recent flood events.
sources.limitations: Some 2023 impact figures are preliminary government estimates; reported averages depend on the underlying event database.

claims.locator: Press-release summary, CCDR headline paragraph on potential economic losses and health costs.
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank summary projects economic losses could reach 17% of GDP by 2050 without reforms, diversification and climate action; it also reports health costs rising from US$92 million in 2010 to US$260 million by 2050.
claims.scenario: Without reforms, diversification and climate action, as stated in the summary; underlying model assumptions are not stated there.
claims.limitations: Summary-level projection; no uncertainty range or underlying scenario specification in the inspected paragraph.

claims.locator: Press-release summary, paragraph on the CCDR’s adaptation priorities.
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank summary lists climate-ready health and education services, disease surveillance, climate-smart agriculture and forest management among proposed priorities; these are recommendations, not verified delivery.
claims.limitations: Reports policy priorities from a summary page only; no implementation or effectiveness evidence is asserted.

claims.locator: Section 3.1.1, subsection b, ‘Sous-secteur de l’hydroélectricité’, printed pp. 23–24 (PDF pp. 22–23).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC assesses hydropower as moderately exposed to climate hazards, particularly uneven rainfall and drought, because generation depends on surface-water availability and river flows.
claims.limitations: This is the NDC’s sectoral exposure assessment; no basin-specific exposure values are supplied in the cited passage.

claims.locator: Section 3.1, impacts and vulnerabilities, printed pp. 23–24 (PDF pp. 23–24), Congo River and coastal-zone discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC describes repeated low river-water levels and identifies coastal flooding, erosion, submersion and salinization among risks to coastal areas; it says sea-level rise was not yet perceptible in the assessment.
claims.limitations: The source’s statement that sea-level rise was not yet perceptible is tied to its 2021 assessment period.

claims.locator: Chapter ‘Flood Events of 2023–2024’, section A, printed p. 65 (PDF p. 65), paragraph 1.
claims.paraphrase: The IMF report says major floods have become more recurrent, affecting the river corridor and Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire; the Congo and Oubangui reached record levels during the 2023–2024 rainy season.
affected_groups: Residents in flood-prone regions and urban centers
claims.limitations: The passage describes recent events and reports drainage, sanitation and construction conditions as impact amplifiers.

claims.locator: Chapter ‘Flood Events of 2023–2024’, section B, printed p. 66 (PDF p. 66), paragraph 3.
claims.paraphrase: For December 2023 floods across nine departments, initial government estimates as of January 2024 counted 336,560 people affected and 23 deaths; homes, schools, health centers, water and sanitation were disrupted, and farming and fishing halted.
geographies: Nine departments, mainly northern regions bordering the Congo River
affected_groups: Households dependent on farming and fishing
institutions: Government of the Republic of Congo
claims.limitations: Impact figures were initial government estimates as of January 2024, as reported by the IMF.

claims.locator: Chapter ‘Flood Events of 2023–2024’, section A, printed p. 65 (PDF p. 65), EM-DAT summary paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: Using EM-DAT data from 2000, the IMF chapter reports a flood about every two and a half years and an average of approximately 92,000 people affected per flood event.
claims.limitations: Historical average based on EM-DAT from 2000; the cited passage does not provide a confidence interval or event-by-event series.

sources.title: The Gambia Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate and agricultural trends; modelled poverty effects to 2050; climate scenarios through the second half of the century
sources.methodology: CCDR combines climate projections with economic, poverty, and development analysis.
sources.limitations: Rainfall projections are indicative; poverty modelling omits some non-labour and disaster-asset effects.

sources.title: The Gambia Floods Rapid Needs Assessment Report
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), with UNDAC and national counterparts
sources.temporal_coverage: Floods of July–August 2022; assessment published January 2023
sources.methodology: Rapid needs assessment drawing on national disaster-management data, a perception survey, and secondary-source review.
sources.limitations: Affected and displaced counts are assessment estimates; the inspected report does not attribute the floods to climate change.

sources.title: The Gambia Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate vulnerability and policy document; dated 2021
sources.methodology: Government NDC describing national climate vulnerabilities and commitments.
sources.limitations: The cited passage is a qualitative national assessment and does not quantify the exposed population or attribute specific impacts.

claims.locator: Chapter on climate and fragility, printed p. 37 (PDF p. 53), discussion of climate shocks, resource scarcity, and conflict drivers.
claims.paraphrase: CCDR warns agricultural shocks may worsen hunger and resource scarcity, heightening conflict risk; weak tenure, dispute resolution and climate capacity compound it.
claims.scenario: No scenario or date specified.
affected_groups: People dependent on agriculture and natural resources
claims.limitations: Qualitative risk, not quantified.

claims.locator: Executive summary, printed p. 15 (PDF p. 32), coastal exposure and agricultural trend paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: Coastal zones with over 60% of the population face sea-level rise, erosion, and salt intrusion; yields declined an estimated 1.2% annually since 2010 amid erratic rain and drought.
claims.limitations: National estimate; no district breakdown.

claims.locator: Climate scenario discussion, printed p. 20 (PDF p. 37), precipitation projections.
claims.paraphrase: SSP5-8.5 projects more severe or prolonged rainy-season dry spells in the second half of the century; rainfall projections are highly variable.
claims.scenario: SSP5-8.5; later-century. Report also compares SSP2-4.5.
claims.limitations: Indicative given high rainfall variability.

claims.locator: Poverty-impact modelling, printed p. 71 (PDF p. 88), 2050 results by climate scenario and adaptation case.
claims.paraphrase: By 2050, modelled poverty rises 1.2 points (dry/hot) or 0.6 (wet/warm) without adaptation, versus 0.4 or 0.2 points with the stated adaptation pathway.
claims.scenario: Dry/hot and wet/warm cases, with/without adaptation; SSP label unstated here.
claims.limitations: Model excludes some non-labour and disaster-asset effects.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF p. 2, affected and displaced population estimates for the July–August 2022 floods.
claims.paraphrase: The rapid assessment estimated that the 2022 floods affected 50,378 people and displaced 7,404 across Greater Banjul, North Bank, Central River, and Upper River regions.
claims.limitations: Rapid assessment estimates; the inspected source does not attribute these floods to climate change.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF p. 3, water and sanitation consequences and rural vulnerability.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment reports that floods breached water and sewage systems and contaminated water bodies. Greater Banjul had the largest number affected, while rural communities were described as more vulnerable.
claims.limitations: The source reports assessment findings and does not provide a causal climate attribution.

claims.locator: Climate vulnerability description, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 5), paragraph on economic vulnerability and coastal ecosystems.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC describes the economy as vulnerable to drought and changes in annual rainfall, and notes that rising temperatures and saltwater intrusion threaten mangroves and increase flood susceptibility.
claims.scenario: The cited qualitative passage does not specify a climate scenario or dated projection.
claims.limitations: Qualitative government vulnerability statement without quantified impacts at this locator.

sources.title: Ghana Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical flood impacts; modelled poverty impacts to 2050
sources.methodology: World Bank CCDR with climate-risk, economic, and poverty analysis.
sources.limitations: The cited poverty effects are modelled; the coastal and annual flood figures are national-level estimates.

sources.title: Climate-Proofing Northern Ghana’s Future: Investing in Resilient Livelihoods and Infrastructure
sources.organization: National Development Planning Commission (Ghana), prepared for the SOCO project
geographic_coverage: 48 districts across five northern regions and Oti Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical droughts 1981–2019; 2024 drought and flood reporting; projection to 2080
sources.methodology: Policy brief reports a mixed-method study with geospatial analysis and interviews involving 210 participants.
sources.limitations: Reported district and event findings are not a national causal estimate; the cited 2080 risk passage does not identify its projection scenario.

sources.title: Ghana’s Updated Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement (2020–2030)
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC policy and implementation period 2020–2030
sources.methodology: Government NDC setting out mitigation and adaptation actions, institutional responsibilities, and intended coverage.
sources.limitations: The beneficiary figure is a planned reach, not an independently verified result.

claims.locator: Executive summary, printed p. xi (PDF p. 11), poverty modelling to 2050.
claims.paraphrase: CCDR modelling estimates climate change could raise Ghana’s poverty rate by 1–2 percentage points by 2050, or leave about one million more people poor than a no-climate-change case.
claims.scenario: CCDR comparison with a no-climate-change case; the cited summary passage does not specify an emissions scenario.
claims.limitations: Modelled scenario, not an observed poverty change.

claims.locator: Printed p. 5 (PDF p. 19), flood and coastal exposure summary.
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR reports about 45,000 people affected by floods annually and identifies roughly half of Ghana’s 550-km coastline as vulnerable to erosion and flooding associated with sea-level rise.
claims.limitations: The cited passage summarizes national estimates without district-level breakdown.

claims.locator: Findings, PDF p. 2 (printed p. 2), climate stress and agriculture in northern Ghana.
claims.paraphrase: Across the study area, respondents most often identified drought (39%), bushfires (22%), and floods (16%) as climate-related concerns; more than 97% of surveyed households engaged in crop farming.
geographies: 48 districts in five northern regions and Oti Region
claims.limitations: Findings describe the study sample and are not a nationally representative prevalence estimate.

claims.locator: Findings, PDF p. 2, reported 2024 drought and recurring Bagre Dam floods.
claims.paraphrase: The brief says a three-month 2024 drought cut yields by about half in affected locations; recurring Bagre Dam floods have displaced communities and damaged farms, homes, and roads.
claims.limitations: The brief’s reported impacts were not independently verified in the inspected passage.

claims.locator: PDF p. 3, concluding discussion of food-system reliability, migration, and conflict risk to 2080.
claims.paraphrase: The brief warns that chronic unreliability in northern food systems could increase migration and conflict risks related to competition over land and water through 2080.
claims.scenario: Projection to 2080; the cited passage does not identify the climate or socioeconomic scenario.
affected_groups: People dependent on northern food systems
claims.limitations: This is a stated prospective risk, not evidence that climate impacts caused migration or conflict; scenario unspecified.

claims.locator: NDC summary and institutional arrangements, printed pp. 3–5, adaptation action and intended reach.
claims.paraphrase: Ghana’s updated NDC sets out 19 policy actions, including 13 adaptation actions, and estimates planned coverage of 38 million people by 2030, mainly women and youth; EPA and NDPC have coordination and planning roles.
claims.scenario: Government implementation plan through 2030; intended coverage, not realized reach.

claims.locator: Section 1.2, printed p. 19 (PDF p. 19), climate-risk profile and scenario tables.
claims.paraphrase: Mean annual warming is projected at 1.1–3.0°C by the 2060s and 1.6–5.3°C by the 2090s, fastest in the north and northwest; 2041–50 dry/hot and wet/warm cases differ in both temperature and rainfall.
claims.scenario: Profile ranges to 2060s/2090s; dry/hot and wet/warm cases compare 2041-50 with 1995-2020; rainfall uncertain.
claims.limitations: The passage notes significant uncertainty in precipitation changes.

claims.locator: Section 1.2, printed p. 19 (PDF p. 19), CC-MFMod results under dry/hot and wet/warm climate scenarios.
claims.paraphrase: Without accelerated adaptation, modelled 2050 GDP losses reach 11.6% under dry/hot conditions and 2.5% under wet/warm conditions.
claims.scenario: CCDR macroeconomic pathways and climate scenarios; cited dry/hot and wet/warm results are without accelerated adaptation.
claims.limitations: Modelled scenario estimates, not observed GDP losses.

claims.locator: Printed p. 18 (PDF p. 18), discussion of fragility, governance, land issues, and intercommunal violence.
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR states that climate impacts aggravate Guinea’s fragility; it also identifies insecure tenure and land issues among fragility drivers linked in the report to rural poverty, gender inequality, and intercommunal violence.
claims.scenario: Qualitative country assessment; no climate scenario or dated projection is specified in this passage.
claims.limitations: Qualitative framing; the passage does not estimate a causal climate effect on violence.

claims.locator: Section on climate risks, printed p. 23 (PDF p. 23), 2024 flood impacts and 2025 events near Conakry.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC lists drought, rainfall disruption, floods, heat, and sea-level rise; it reports 132,496 flood-affected people in 2024 and further major flooding near Conakry in summer 2025.
claims.limitations: Government-reported count; independent validation not inspected.

claims.locator: Printed p. 24 (PDF p. 24), socio-economic effects, climate-related internal mobility, and adaptation needs.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC says climate impacts interact with socioeconomic fragilities and contribute to internal mobility toward Conakry; it describes migration as a frequently cited adaptation strategy.
claims.limitations: Qualitative association; no migration count or causal estimate.

claims.locator: Printed p. 24 (PDF p. 24), coastal exposure and mangrove adaptation needs.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC names Conakry, Forécariah, Boffa, and Kamsar as exposed to coastal inundation, erosion, and saline intrusion; it calls for risk mapping and 5,000 hectares of mangrove restoration.
claims.scenario: Risk mapping to 2030/2050; scenario unstated.
claims.limitations: Needs and plans, not completed results.

claims.locator: Printed p. 23 (PDF p. 23), proposed adaptation governance for 2026–2035.
claims.paraphrase: For 2026–2035, the NDC proposes interministerial and municipal coordination, local contingency plans, inclusive committees with at least 40% women, and linked early-warning and assistance protocols.
claims.scenario: Proposed NDC governance arrangements for 2026–2035.
institutions: National Agency for Economic and Social Inclusion
claims.limitations: Proposals only; implementation and performance unverified.

claims.locator: Section 5.6, printed p. 58 (PDF p. 62), coastal and marine climate risks.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC says coastal and marine ecosystems face storms, flooding, erosion and sea-level rise, with growing freshwater scarcity and declining marine productivity.
claims.scenario: Qualitative long-term hazards; no climate scenario is specified at this locator.
affected_groups: People dependent on coastal and marine ecosystems
claims.limitations: Qualitative projection; no scenario or quantified future loss at this locator.

claims.locator: Section 5.6, printed p. 58 (PDF p. 62), mangrove coverage and change.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports mangroves cover about 22% of the country and declined approximately 19% in 2001–2021; they support fisheries and many livelihoods.
claims.limitations: The reported decline is not attributed wholly to climate change in the passage.

claims.locator: Section 5.6, printed p. 58 (PDF p. 62), adaptation action A21.1 and its 2035 targets.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC proposes 50 km of coastal and riverine anti-salt dykes by 2035, prioritizing high-risk areas with predominantly women residents; mangrove restoration is also targeted.
claims.scenario: Government NDC target for 2035; the passage also proposes mangrove restoration targets.
geographies: Coastal and riverine high-risk areas of Guinea-Bissau
claims.limitations: Proposed targets, not completed works or verified protection outcomes.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF p. 3, adaptation vulnerability and priority regions.
claims.paraphrase: NC4 identifies vulnerabilities in coastal, Bijagós, inland agricultural, and riverside areas, linked to poverty, natural-resource dependence, and institutional and infrastructure weaknesses.
claims.limitations: National assessment; no subnational impact rates in this summary passage.

claims.locator: Section 4.7, PDF p. 118, reported losses and damages.
claims.paraphrase: NC4 reports coastal displacement from land and housing loss, farmer crop failures amid unpredictable rainfall, and threats to Bijagós ecosystems.
claims.limitations: Losses are not quantified by affected households at this locator.

claims.locator: Section 4.7, PDF p. 118, institutional response challenges.
claims.paraphrase: NC4 identifies weak cross-sector coordination, insufficient data and climate finance, and a lack of compensation or insurance mechanisms for climate-related loss and damage.
claims.limitations: Challenges are as reported by NC4, not an independent performance score.

claims.locator: Section 2.3, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 10), regional 2016–2045 climate projections.
claims.paraphrase: For 2016–2045, the NDC projects coastal warming of 1.2°C under RCP4.5 and 1.3°C under RCP8.5, versus 1.4°C and 1.5°C inland; rainfall is projected to rise slightly or stagnate, with local exceptions.
claims.limitations: The NDC notes climate variability; projection uncertainty is not quantified in this passage.

claims.locator: Section 2.3, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 11), interior and coastal impacts.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC describes the interior as prone to longer droughts, fires, floods, and water shortages; the coastal zone holds about 70% of the population and faces saline intrusion in agricultural fields.
claims.scenario: Qualitative regional risk description; scenario not specified at this locator.
claims.limitations: Qualitative impacts are not quantified by region in the cited passage.

claims.locator: Section 3.1.6, printed p. 73 (PDF p. 73), modeled poverty impact under climate scenarios.
claims.paraphrase: The G5 CCDR projects that under medium growth and its dry/pessimistic climate scenario without adaptation, Mauritania’s poverty rate in 2050 would be 0.2 percentage points above the no-climate baseline.
claims.scenario: Medium-growth baseline with dry/pessimistic climate scenario; no adaptation.
claims.limitations: The reported change is relative to the no-climate baseline and uses 2017 household-survey data in a macro-microsimulation.

sources.title: Contribution Déterminée au Niveau National du Sénégal: Document approuvé – décembre 2020
sources.organization: Republic of Senegal; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Government NDC climate-risk projections and adaptation commitments through 2030
sources.methodology: Government NDC summarizes observed climate impacts and modeled regional climate risks.
sources.limitations: NDC projections are dated and should not be read as current observations or as evaluated results.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 4), modeled cost of inaction.
claims.paraphrase: Summary models no-adaptation annual losses at 3-4% GDP by 2030 and 9.4% by 2050; over two million people could fall into poverty by mid-century.
claims.scenario: No adaptation; SSP/RCP unstated here.
claims.limitations: Modeled, not observed.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 4), adaptation scenario results.
claims.paraphrase: Selected-sector adaptation could add about 2% GDP by 2030 and reduce climate-induced poverty by 45% versus no action.
claims.scenario: Selected adaptation versus no action; assumptions unstated.
claims.limitations: Modeled scenario, not program evaluation.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 6), coastal exposure.
claims.paraphrase: Half of Senegal's population and two-thirds of GDP face sea-level exposure; Dakar's population at coastal-flood risk is projected to rise 20-30% by 2050.
claims.scenario: Scenario not specified here.
claims.limitations: National exposure and Dakar change; no district detail.

claims.locator: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 20 (PDF p. 21), historical drought impacts on agriculture and food security.
claims.paraphrase: The diagnostic reports that the 2002 drought reduced agricultural production by about 35% and the 2011 drought by 20%; estimated production losses across 12 major crops during 1980–2020 totaled FCFA 852 billion, averaging 3.9% of agricultural GDP annually.
claims.limitations: Historical estimates combine reported episodes and statistical analysis across 12 crops; the report notes modeled risk robustness depends on input data.

claims.locator: Section 3.7, printed p. 28 (PDF p. 29), forward climate-risk analysis.
claims.paraphrase: The diagnostic says northern Senegal is projected to experience more frequent extreme droughts, particularly in Saint-Louis; its cited CCDR scenarios estimate annual GDP losses of 3.6–4% by 2030 and 7–9.4% by 2050 without adaptation.
claims.scenario: Climate projections for northern drought; cited CCDR GDP range varies by warming assumption and assumes no adaptation.
claims.limitations: GDP figures are from the separate Senegal CCDR, cited by this diagnostic; they are not observed losses.

claims.locator: Section I, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 3), observed impacts and climate-risk projections.
claims.paraphrase: Senegal’s NDC reports declining rainfall, rising mean temperature, sea-level rise, and disruptions to cultivable land, water, and fisheries; it identifies northern regions, especially Saint-Louis, as facing a 20–30% increase in extreme-drought frequency, and identifies more wet extremes in Matam, Tambacounda, and Louga under its low-warming scenario.
claims.scenario: NDC low-warming scenario for wet extremes; drought-frequency scenario is not further labeled in the cited summary.
affected_groups: People whose livelihoods depend on natural resources
claims.limitations: This is a 2020 NDC projection; the summarized model passage does not name an RCP/SSP or projection year.

sources.title: NDC 3.0 of the Republic of Sierra Leone
sources.organization: Republic of Sierra Leone; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC 3.0 risk analysis and planned climate actions for 2025-2035
sources.methodology: Government NDC presents a qualitative conflict-sensitive climate-risk framework and adaptation measures.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. xii (PDF p. 14), climate-risk projections; chapter 1, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 22), rainfall baseline and uncertainty.
claims.paraphrase: Prolonged dry spells and intense heavy rainfall are projected, but rainfall direction and magnitude remain uncertain; mean precipitation was 2,653.4 mm in 1991-2020.
claims.scenario: Multiple climate scenarios; the report describes both hotter/drier and warmer/wetter futures.
claims.limitations: Projections vary across models, seasons, and regions.

claims.locator: Section 3.3, printed p. 30 (PDF p. 46), poverty impacts by climate scenario.
claims.paraphrase: Without adaptation, rural poverty is projected to rise 6.5-6.9 percentage points by 2050 under hot/dry or wet/warm scenarios, versus about 1.5 points in urban areas.
claims.scenario: Baseline-growth, no-adaptation hot/dry and wet/warm climate scenarios.
claims.limitations: Changes are relative to baseline, not absolute poverty rates.

claims.locator: Section 3.3, printed p. 31 (PDF p. 47), district poverty results.
claims.paraphrase: Climate change could erase Port Loko's poverty gains by about 12 points by 2050 under either case; Kambia and Bonthe also face wet/warm impacts.
claims.scenario: Hot/dry and wet/warm; baseline growth, no adaptation.
claims.limitations: Port Loko change is relative to poverty-reduction baseline.

claims.locator: Section 4.2, printed p. 79 (PDF p. 80), flood exposure of schools.
claims.paraphrase: 372,000 children (11% of students) faced school-flood exposure; 10% of schools flooded repeatedly, and Bonthe had the highest district exposure and vulnerability.
institutions: Ministry of Basic and Senior Secondary Education
claims.limitations: Observed school floods are not attributed to climate change.

claims.locator: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 28 (PDF p. 136), conflict-sensitive climate risks.
claims.paraphrase: Sierra Leone’s NDC states that, in its post-conflict context, climate-related livelihood insecurity, resource competition, and migration can act as threat multipliers that heighten social-unrest or renewed-conflict risks, especially for youth and marginalized groups.
claims.scenario: Qualitative NDC risk framing for fragile contexts; no quantified scenario is specified.
claims.limitations: This is an NDC risk statement, not quantified causal evidence or a local conflict-event assessment.

claims.locator: Section 3.2.2 and Table 50, printed p. 28 (PDF pp. 136-137), pastoralist-farmer risk pathway and response priorities.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC describes a risk in which drought and erratic rainfall may push herders beyond traditional grazing areas onto farmland, potentially triggering violent disputes over shrinking resources; its stated priorities include integrated land-use planning, formal land rights, migration corridors, and local mediation involving traditional leaders, youth, and women.
claims.scenario: Qualitative risk pathway; NDC table gives no quantified likelihood, place-specific forecast, or event date.
claims.limitations: The NDC frames a potential mechanism and proposed measures; it does not establish this as an observed countrywide pathway.

sources.methodology: Government NDC summarizes sector risks, losses and climate projections using cited assessments.
sources.limitations: Several quantified flood and fishery estimates are attributed to external studies, not new NDC analysis.

sources.title: Prosperity for All Saotomeans: Priorities to End Poverty, Promote Growth, and Build Resilience in São Tomé and Príncipe - Systematic Country Diagnostic
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate observations from 1951 to 2010 and country diagnostic published in 2021
sources.methodology: World Bank diagnostic synthesizes country and sector evidence; trends draw on the Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal.
sources.limitations: Climate trends are historical and based on polynomial fits; they do not represent updated observations.

claims.locator: Section 4.3, PDF p. 67 (one-based), flood and landslide loss-and-damage summary.
claims.paraphrase: NDC reports December 2021-February 2022 floods and landslides damaged infrastructure, agriculture and WASH; recovery cost $37.5m, about 7% of 2022 GDP.
claims.limitations: NDC attributes the recovery estimate to an IFRC 2024 country plan.

claims.locator: Section 4.3.1, PDF p. 68 (one-based), projected economic losses.
claims.paraphrase: NDC cites annual flood losses rising from 1.9% of GDP in 2020 to 2.8% by 2050 and 4.1% by 2080.
claims.scenario: Cited assessment incorporates RCP4.5 and RCP8.5; NDC does not assign the loss figures to one pathway.
claims.limitations: Figures are reproduced from the World Bank's 2024 national flood-risk assessment.

claims.locator: Section 4.1.2, PDF p. 51 (one-based), fisheries exposure and impacts.
claims.paraphrase: NDC states fisheries provide 70-85% of animal protein and support 15% of active workers; extreme weather and erosion damage boats and isolate communities.
claims.limitations: Fisheries baseline figures are attributed to World Bank 2017.

claims.locator: Section 4.1.2, PDF p. 52 (one-based), artisanal fishing and maritime-crime discussion.
claims.paraphrase: NDC says falling catches push artisanal fishers farther offshore; Gulf of Guinea evidence elsewhere suggests maritime-crime exposure and fleet competition may rise.
claims.limitations: Crime-risk link is analogical evidence from elsewhere, not measured local incidence.

claims.locator: Chapter 3, printed pp. 70-71 (PDF pp. 85-86), coastal hazards and exposed infrastructure.
claims.paraphrase: SCD reports recurrent floods, landslides, erosion and storms threaten lives, livelihoods, the airport and primary roads concentrated along the coast.
claims.limitations: Diagnostic describes exposure, not asset-level damage probabilities.

claims.locator: Chapter 3, printed p. 72 (PDF p. 87), historical climate observations.
claims.paraphrase: World Bank climate data show 1951-2010 warming of 1.5°C, mean rainfall falling 1.7 mm yearly, and March-May rainfall dropping 10.5 mm monthly.
claims.limitations: Historical trends use Climate Change Knowledge Portal data and polynomial fits.

access_audit.notes: Opened substantive fisheries and loss-and-damage passages in the full UNFCCC-hosted NDC.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Publisher reuse terms were not independently confirmed; no source wording reproduced.

sources.title: Première Communication relative à l'Adaptation aux Changements Climatiques au Togo
sources.organization: Ministère de l'Environnement et des Ressources Forestières, République Togolaise
sources.temporal_coverage: Synthesis of 2017-2023 vulnerability studies; projections to 2050 and 2100
sources.methodology: Government communication synthesizes assessments, document review, stakeholder consultations and field visits.
sources.limitations: Regional indices summarize cited sector studies rather than one unified underlying dataset.

sources.title: Contributions Déterminées au Niveau National Révisées du Togo: Document Intérimaire
sources.organization: Ministère de l'Environnement et des Ressources Forestières, République Togolaise
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical sector impacts and climate observations; basin and sector projections to 2030 and 2050
sources.methodology: Interim revised NDC compiles climate projections, sector vulnerability assessments and reported impacts.
sources.limitations: Sector figures cite distinct studies and periods; climate-conflict links are not causal event analyses.

claims.locator: Executive summary, printed p. iii (PDF p. 3), agriculture vulnerability by region.
claims.paraphrase: Agriculture vulnerability is high nationwide and very high in Savanes; under RCP6.0, Kara also reaches very high by 2050.
claims.scenario: RCP6.0; projection horizon 2050.
claims.limitations: Indices summarize cited studies; no uncertainty intervals are stated.

claims.locator: Section 2.3.4.1, printed p. 50 (PDF p. 61), coastal erosion and shoreline change.
claims.paraphrase: Communication reports retreat along 40 km of sandy coast at an average 10 m yearly, aggravated by storms and local sediment dynamics.
claims.limitations: The communication cites WACA ResIP-Togo coastal research for this measurement.

claims.locator: Section 2.3.4.1, printed p. 50 (PDF p. 61), sea-level projection summary.
claims.paraphrase: Under RCP6.0, sea level is projected to rise 11.35 cm by 2025 and 62 cm by 2100, worsening coastal erosion and livelihood risks.
claims.scenario: RCP6.0.
claims.limitations: Reproduced from Togo's 2019 national communication; 2025 remains a dated projection, not an observed sea level.

claims.locator: Section 4.2.2.2, PDF pp. 50-51 (one-based), livestock vulnerability and farmer-herder conflict.
claims.paraphrase: NDC links prolonged drought in recent decades with recurring farmer-herder conflicts in the Savanes and Plateaux livestock areas.
claims.limitations: Report states recurring conflict alongside drought but provides no causal event analysis.

claims.locator: Section 4.2.3, PDF pp. 51-52 (one-based), basin water projections and source-conflict risk.
claims.paraphrase: Under RCP6.0 to 2030, water stocks rise in Mono but fall in Oti and Lake Togo; NDC warns inaction may heighten water-source conflict risk.
claims.scenario: RCP6.0 stabilization; horizon 2030.
claims.limitations: Modeled basin changes and stated conflict risk are not a forecast of violent incidents.

claims.locator: Section 4.2.4, PDF p. 52 (one-based), Oti and Mono flood impacts in 2020 and 2021.
claims.paraphrase: NDC reports 2020-2021 Oti and Mono floods caused deaths and damaged roads, markets, health centers, homes, schools, power and telecoms.
claims.limitations: NDC summarizes impacts without event-level loss totals.

claims.locator: Section 4.2.2.2, PDF p. 50 (one-based), 2020 crop losses from flooding and dry spells.
claims.paraphrase: NDC estimates 6,902 hectares of food crops flooded in 2020 and production losses near 9,000 tonnes; dry spells also reduced yields.
claims.limitations: Figures summarize referenced assessments and impacts for the stated period.

access_audit.locator: 159-page communication; executive summary p. iii and section 2.3.4.1, printed p. 50 (PDF p. 61).
access_audit.notes: Opened substantive regional agriculture and coastal vulnerability passages in the full government report.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Report states © République Togolaise 2023; no source wording reproduced.
